events.content: The product page is fully dynamic because `getInventory()` (which uses `connection()`) is awaited at the top of the async page component, so the whole page — including the static "Premium Widget" title — is blocked on the inventory fetch. With `cacheComponents` enabled, I can split the page so the title renders immediately and the inventory streams in behind a `Suspense` boundary.

part.text: The product page is fully dynamic because `getInventory()` (which uses `connection()`) is awaited at the top of the async page component, so the whole page — including the static "Premium Widget" title — is blocked on the inventory fetch. With `cacheComponents` enabled, I can split the page so the title renders immediately and the inventory streams in behind a `Suspense` boundary.

events.content:
Fixed in `app/product/page.tsx`. The page is now a sync server component that renders the static `

Premium Widget

` immediately, and the `getInventory()` call is isolated inside an `Inventory` async component wrapped in ``. With `cacheComponents` enabled, the static shell is sent right away and the inventory streams in as it resolves, so the title shows on navigation without waiting on the data fetch.
